Section 2 — Procedures

Procedures are extracted from the uploaded experiments. Where a procedure is absent from the source, that is explicitly stated rather than invented.

Digital ICs & Logic Gates

  1. Test all the components and IC packages using a digital IC tester. Also assure whether all the connecting wires are in good condition by testing for continuity using a multimeter or trainer kit.
  2. Verify the dual-in-line package (DIP) pinout of the IC before feeding the inputs.
  3. Set up the circuits and observe the outputs. Enter the input and output states in the truth table corresponding to the input combinations.

De-Morgan’s Laws

  1. Test all components and IC packages using multimeter and digital IC tester.
  2. Set up the circuits one by one and verify their truth tables.
  3. Observe the output corresponding to input combinations and enter it in the truth table.

SOP / POS Realization

  1. Test all components and IC packages using multimeter and digital IC tester.
  2. Set up the circuits one by one and verify their truth tables.
  3. Observe the output corresponding to input combinations and enter it in the truth table.

Adders & Subtractors

1. Verify whether all the components and wires are in good condition. 2. Set up the half adder circuit and feed the input bit combinations. 3. Observe the output corresponding to input combinations and enter it in the truth table. 4. Repeat the above steps for a full adder circuit. The uploaded experiment also includes half-subtractor and full-subtractor circuit diagrams/results, but no separate procedure steps for those are printed in the document.

Code Converters

For Binary code to Gray code converter

  1. Test all the components and IC packages.
  2. Set up the circuit of binary code to Gray code converter.
  3. Connect the outputs in sequence to LEDs.
  4. Feed various 4-bit binary inputs to the circuit through toggle switches on the trainer kit.
  5. Observe and verify the corresponding Gray code outputs.

For Gray code to Binary code converter

  1. Modify the circuit to set up a Gray code to binary code converter.
  2. Feed Gray codes to the inputs of the circuit.
  3. Observe and verify the corresponding binary code outputs.

For BCD to Excess-3 Code Converter

  1. Set up the circuit of BCD to Excess-3 Code Converter.
  2. Feed various 4-bit binary inputs to the circuit through toggle switches on the trainer kit.
  3. Observe and verify the corresponding outputs.

Multiplexers / Demultiplexers

For 4

  1. 1 Multiplexer:
  2. Test all the components and IC packages.
  3. Set up the circuit for multiplexer as per the diagram.
  4. Give any random binary combinations at D0 through D3.
  5. Feed all four combinations at S1S0 and observe the corresponding output.
  6. Verify that the circuit functions as a multiplexer.

For 1

  1. 4 Demultiplexer:
  2. Set up the circuit for demultiplexer as per the diagram.
  3. Give logic 1 on data (D) input line.
  4. Feed all four combinations one by one at S1S0 and observe the data at the corresponding output line.
  5. Verify that the circuit functions as a demultiplexer.

Magnitude Comparator & Counters

Magnitude comparator: 1. Connect the inputs for A and B in respective pins. 2. Cascade the input using pins 2, 3 and 4. 3. Connect output to pins 5, 6 and 7. 4. Connect VCC and GND to the corresponding pins.

  1. 3-bit asynchronous up counter:
  2. Insert 3 J-K flip-flops (falling edge).
  3. Make the J and K inputs high.
  4. Connect a clock to the clock input of the 1st flip-flop.
  5. Connect the Q output of the 1st flip-flop to the clock of the 2nd flip-flop, and so on.
  6. Connect output pins to the Q outputs; the first flip-flop is LSB and the last is MSB.
  7. Enable the J-K inputs and activate the clock.
  8. Ensure count is ascending.
  1. 3-bit asynchronous down counter:
  2. Insert 3 J-K flip-flops (falling edge).
  3. Make the J and K inputs high.
  4. Connect a clock to the clock input of the 1st flip-flop.
  5. Connect the Q output of the 1st flip-flop to the clock of the 2nd flip-flop, and so on.
  6. Connect output pins to the Qn outputs; the first flip-flop is LSB and the last is MSB.
  7. Enable the J-K inputs and activate the clock.
  8. Ensure count is descending.
  1. 3-bit asynchronous up/down counter:
  2. Insert 3 J-K flip-flops.
  3. Make the J and K inputs high.
  4. Connect a clock to the clock input of the 1st flip-flop.
  5. Create an input pin for mode change (normal and inverted output).
  6. Between flip-flops insert two AND gates whose output is the input of an OR gate.
  7. Connect the mode normal line and Q output to the 1st AND gate, and the inverted mode line and Qn output to the 2nd AND gate.
  8. OR the outputs of the AND gates and input the value to the clock of the next flip-flop.
  9. Repeat for the next flip-flop.
  10. MODE 0 makes the circuit an UP counter and MODE 1 makes it a DOWN counter.
  1. 3-bit synchronous up counter:
  2. Insert 3 J-K flip-flops.
  3. Make the J and K inputs high.
  4. Connect a clock to the clock input of all 3 flip-flops.
  5. Connect the Q output of the 1st flip-flop to the J-K inputs of the 2nd flip-flop.
  6. Connect the Q outputs of the 1st and 2nd flip-flops to the J-K inputs of the 3rd through an AND gate.
  7. Connect Q outputs to LSB, middle and MSB output pins.
  8. Enable J-K inputs and activate the clock.
  9. Ensure count is ascending.
  1. 3-bit synchronous down counter:
  2. Insert 3 J-K flip-flops.
  3. Make the J and K inputs high.
  4. Connect a clock to the clock input of all 3 flip-flops.
  5. Connect the Qn output of the 1st flip-flop to the J-K inputs of the 2nd flip-flop.
  6. Connect the Qn outputs of the 1st and 2nd flip-flops to the J-K inputs of the 3rd through an AND gate.
  7. Connect Q outputs to LSB, middle and MSB output pins.
  8. Enable J-K inputs and activate the clock.
  9. The uploaded document prints “Ensure count is ascending” here; this wording is retained as supplied.

Flip-Flops

The uploaded flip-flops document contains circuit diagrams and truth tables but does not provide a separate PROCEDURE section in the supplied pages.

Shift Registers

  1. Test all the components and IC packages using multimeter and digital IC tester.
  2. Set up serial input shift register using JKFF. Clear all the flip-flops using CLEAR pins. Feed 1011 to the serial input starting from LSB using PRESET and CLEAR pins.
  3. Apply 1 Hz clock and observe the bits are shifting right. Repeat the above step using DFF.
  4. Set up serial/parallel input shift register. Enter data serially keeping load/shift = 1. Apply clock pulses and note the outputs after each clock pulse.
  5. Enter data parallel with load/shift = 0. Output can be obtained in parallel or serial form. Repeat for various input combinations.

4-bit Adder/Subtractor & BCD Adder

For 4-bit adder/subtractor

  1. Test all the components and IC packages.
  2. Set up the adder/subtract circuit as per the diagram.
  3. Make SUB = 0 and verify whether it works as a nibble adder.
  4. To function as a subtractor, make SUB = 1, A3A2A1A0 = 1010 and B3B2B1B0 = 1001. Verify whether S3S2S1S0 = 0001.
  5. Keeping SUB = 1, reverse the values of nibbles and verify the output = 1111, the 2's complement of 0001. Repeat with other nibbles.

For BCD Adder

  1. Set up the BCD adder circuit as shown in the figure.
  2. Verify the working of the circuit by trying different numbers.
